**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — Assignment and change of control**

- **Section 20(d) (p0142)** is a flat mutual prohibition on assignment without the other party's written consent — no affiliate carve-out, no successor/M&A carve-out, and no "not to be unreasonably withheld" standard. That fails the fallback position and, on the missing M&A carve-out, is walk-away territory.
- **Section 3(c) (p0033)** compounds this by separately barring Sparkling from assigning the Agreement except as Garman authorizes in writing — an asymmetric restriction on us only.
- **No change-of-control trigger exists**: I checked Section 17 (termination) and searched for "control" — Garman has no termination or re-pricing right on our change of control, so nothing to delete there.

**Redline (validated, ok:true)**: rewrites 20(d) to let Sparkling assign to an affiliate or successor in a merger/acquisition/sale of substantially all assets on written notice; keeps Garman's assignment consent-based (not unreasonably withheld, never to a Sparkling competitor); applies a reasonableness standard to all other assignments; and conforms 3(c) so the use restrictions don't cut across the new right.
